largestHolders.name: National Development Fund, Executive Yuan (R.O.C. government)

structure.note: One class of common shares. The 20-F lists only one holder of 5% or more, the National Development Fund of the Executive Yuan (6.38% at 28 February 2026); directors and executive officers as a group held 0.23% (excluding the Fund). 5,313,450,863 common shares were represented by ADSs held through Citibank, N.A. as depositary.

geography.basis: Net revenue categorized mainly based on the countries where the customers are headquartered

notes: All figures from TSMC's FY2025 Form 20-F (fiscal year ended 31 December 2025; accession 0001628280-26-025362, filed April 16, 2026), read on www.sec.gov. Amounts are NT$ (ISO TWD) millions converted to billions. FOUNDER: Morris Chang retired in 2018. His name does not appear anywhere in the FY2025 20-F (Item 6 directors and officers and Item 7 major shareholders were checked), so status is no-reported-stake. HOLDERS: the National Development Fund (6.38%) is the only 5%+ holder in the 20-F. The 2025 English annual report's top-ten shareholder list (which in the previous edition gave the Government of Singapore and Norges Bank custody accounts) could not be fetched: investor.tsmc.com returns HTTP 403 to scripted requests (Cloudflare), so those holders are not listed this year. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line 'Treasury stock acquired' is nil for 2025 and Item 16E says 'Not applicable', so buybacks are 0. DIVIDENDS: cash-flow line 'Cash dividends' (NT$466,779.2 million paid in 2025); it differs from the NT$531,618.4 million declared in the equity statement because quarterly dividends are paid about six months after approval. STOCK COMP: equity-settled share-based compensation (NT$1,246.1 million, cash-flow add-back). The employee-benefits note also lists NT$304.1 million of cash-settled share-based payments, which are paid in cash and excluded; TSMC's much larger employee profit-sharing bonuses are cash and are not counted here. GEOGRAPHY: from the notes to the financial statements, by customer headquarters country. XBRL: companyfacts carries no FY2025 financial facts for TSMC (only the cover share count), so no xbrl objects are given.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: 'Income taxes paid' in operating activities of the IFRS cash-flow statement; the caption does not say whether refunds are netted. R&D: the operating-expense line in the statement of profit or loss. Companyfacts has no FY2025 financial facts for TSMC, so no xbrl objects are given.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F, accession 0001628280-26-025362). IFRS statements as filed in the 20-F (NT$; the US$ column is a convenience translation, not used). Income taxes paid are inside operating activities (not added); interest paid is in financing (added). Interest received (98,954.7) and dividends received are in investing, so they do not lower OCF. Capex is gross of the 76,258.8 of PP&E government grants received, which sit as a separate investing inflow. Companyfacts has no FY2025 financial facts for TSMC, so no xbrl objects are given.

marketcap.notes: One class of common shares, priced on the primary Taiwan Stock Exchange line (2330.TW) in NT$ rather than the NYSE ADS (TSM, one ADS = five common shares). The count is 'Capital stock (in thousands)' at September 30, 2026 from the third-quarter consolidated report filed on Form 6-K, which excludes 5 thousand reclaimed restricted shares awaiting retirement; it is stated in thousands, so it is rounded to the nearest thousand shares. It is newer than the 20-F count (25,932,524,521 at February 28, 2026), and no buyback, split or tender has changed it materially.

pay.notes: Employees: full-time employees at December 31, 2025, from the 20-F's Item 6.D table (consolidated). Payroll: the IFRS note's total employee benefits expense for 2025 (NT$396,114.8 million: post-employment benefits 6,964.3, share-based payments 1,550.2 and other employee benefits 387,600.3, which include employee profit-sharing bonuses), recognized in cost of revenue (235,604.0) and operating expenses (160,510.8). TSMC is a foreign private issuer and has no CEO pay ratio.
